root_cause_criterion.criterion: Immediately before `TMS320C64x_insn_name()` indexes `insn_name_maps`, the lookup id must be strictly smaller than the actual `insn_name_maps` array length, not merely below the enum sentinel `TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable run reaches the lookup with a valid public TMS320C64x enum value while the vulnerable `insn_name_maps` declaration has only three contiguous elements. The fixed run executes the same lookup with the completed table, so the missing array-bounds conjunct becomes true before the same protected event.
root_cause_criterion.evidence: The vulnerable trace records `name_guard.lookup_id` against `name_guard.insn_name_map_count=3` and still reaches `name_lookup`; the fixed trace reaches the same `name_lookup` event with `name_guard.insn_name_map_count=145`.

nodes.description: At the violating read, `TMS320C64x_insn_name()` uses the carried `id` directly as the raw `insn_name_maps` subscript in `return insn_name_maps[id].name;`.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable trace reaches `name_lookup` after the false bounds predicate at `name_guard`, and the fixed trace reaches the same `name_lookup` event only when the completed table makes that predicate true.

nodes.description: At the source-level sanitizer sink, the pointer returned by `cs_insn_name(handle, i->id)` becomes the final `%s` argument to `fprintf()` in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()`.
nodes.evidence: Both frozen traces record `print_sink.lookup_name_ptr`, showing that the `%s` sink executed with the returned instruction-name pointer.

edges.relation: After the sentinel-only guard admits the call, the same `id` is used unchanged as the subscript in the subsequent `insn_name_maps[id]` lookup.
edges.evidence: Both traces record the same `lookup_id` value at `name_guard` and `name_lookup`.

edges.relation: The pointer read at `return insn_name_maps[id].name;` is returned unchanged through `cs_insn_name(handle, i->id)` and becomes the final `%s` argument at `fprintf()`.
The public TMS320C64x instruction enum written to `insn->id` at `TMS320C64x_get_insn_id()` later arrives unchanged as the `id` argument checked by `TMS320C64x_insn_name()`.
edges.evidence: Both traces record the same instruction-id value at `id_mapped.public_insn_id` and `name_guard.lookup_id`.
